items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I remember one time we had Charlie Christian upstairs, right?

ctx.x: We forced their hands because they had me before the Board so much where you couldn't jam, but they had a practice hall above the union, you know, at 1710 -- and all the people were doing business downstairs, but you could rehearse upstairs.

Well, no one ever rehearsed upstairs until like, six o'clock in the evening, when the union closed at five o'clock. And so they gave me so much heat and static about jamming, so I got the guys together -- there was Blanton, there was Nat -- and this time, really, I remember one time we had Charlie Christian upstairs, right?

And so I started calling the guys, and we started jamming, you know, and Eddie Barefield and Don -- and we started jamming in the day time at the union, and we would start at noon; we would start at 12 o'clock every day. And it would just drive the people crazy downstairs, you know?
